decision_algebra: ANY DENY > ANY INDETERMINATE > ALL PASS

theorem.statement: Creation provenance is admissible only when the TPM creation record, its parent identity, the created AK identity, the TPM-produced creation hash/ticket, and the CertifyCreation attestation all bind to the same session.
required_relations: creation_data.parent_name equals the observed EK Name
creation_data.parent_qualified_name equals the observed EK Qualified Name
creation_record.object_name equals the observed AK Name
creation_record.object_public_sha256 equals the observed AK public digest
creation_record.creation_ticket is recorded as TPM-produced material
certification.certified_object_name equals the created AK Name
creation-data PCR/locality/outsideInfo context is retained rather than discarded

wire_format_boundary: v0.1 requires hashes and parsed fields from the TPM creation-data output; it does not claim to independently re-marshal and hash TPMS_CREATION_DATA from the JSON representation. The captured creation-data wire bytes remain the authoritative input for future wire-level parsing.

required_input.tpm_identity_digest: sha256 digest identifying the capture TPM context

future_live_capture_requirements: use tpm2_create or an equivalent TPM2_Create path with --creation-data, --creation-hash and --creation-ticket outputs
retain the raw creation-data wire bytes and compute their SHA-256 independently of any rendered representation
read the created AK public area, Name and Qualified Name from the TPM
execute tpm2_certifycreation with an explicitly trusted signing-key lineage
retain the TPM2_CREATION attestation structure, signature, qualifying data, and ticket-validation result
bind the creation certificate to the same session and TPM identity as AK/EK credential activation and Quote
